name: germline_nuclei_combined
what: Cellpose-SAM fine-tuned on real hand-labelled germline nuclei plus synthetic nuclei (June 2026): the recommended nucleus model, used by every validated run. Runs at native scale (diameter is ignored for cpsam-derived models).
pixel_um_note: not recorded in the release record

training.data: 48 real hand-labelled germline nucleus slices (data/train_kohler) plus about 49 synthetic slices (every 4th of 198, data/train_nuclei), about 1:1
training.network: CellposeModel(gpu=True).net: Cellpose's default network and weights at training time

holdout_metrics.source: config/config.yaml (segmentation.nuclei comment) and docs; not recomputed for this card

base_model.name: not determined
base_model.date_evidence: File dates point to cpsam_v2: it was cached on 2026-06-12, the model is dated 2026-06-13, the training script builds CellposeModel(gpu=True), whose default in Cellpose 4.2.x is cpsam_v2, and the cpsam (v1) cache file dates from 2026-09-24. Dates do not prove the base.

comparison.method: tensor-by-tensor comparison of the fine-tuned state dict with each candidate base state dict (germquant.packs.basecheck): bit-identical tensors and the relative L2 distance ||model - base|| / ||base|| over the tensors the two share with the same shape; the closest base is named only when it covers at least 90% of the model's tensors and the next base is at least 2 times farther
comparison.how: python scripts/compare_base_weights.py --write (on the workstation, CPU only; it writes the result here and rebuilds SHA256SUMS)

licence_note: Cellpose-SAM weights are BSD-3-Clause; Cellpose's own training data is distributed under a non-commercial (CC BY-NC) licence, so a model fine-tuned from cpsam inherits that question for commercial use (README, License).
